questions.question: In which of the following years was the origin and enactment of the Indian Age of Consent Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1891**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Age of Consent Act was legislation enacted in British India on 19 March 1891 that raised the age of consent for sexual intercourse from ten to twelve years for all girls in all jurisdictions**__.

 
 
• The Act was also known as Act X of 1891.
 
• It was an amendment to the Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, Section 375, 1882.
 
• Parishad member Sir Romesh Chunder Mitter (from Bengal) opposed it on the grounds that it interfered with the orthodox Hindu code.
 
• However, it received support from Indian reformers such as Behramji Malabari and women's social organizations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a private good?

options.text: A good that is consumed by a single person or household
A good that is available to everyone to consume, regardless of who pays for it and who does not.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A good that is consumed by a single person or household**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A good that is consumed by a single person or household is a private good**__. 

 
 
• A public good is a product that one individual can consume without reducing its availability to others and from which no one is excluded.
 
• A private good is the opposite of a public good.
 
• A private good is a product that must be purchased to be consumed, and consumption by one individual prevents another individual from consuming it.
 
• We encounter private goods every day. For example- dinner at a restaurant, grocery shopping, airplane rides, and cellphones.
 
• Any item that is effectively destroyed or rendered unusable for its original purpose through use, such as food and toilet paper, are also private good.

questions.question: Of the known elements in the periodic table, only _______ are gases under normal atmospheric conditions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Of the known elements in the periodic table, only 11 are gases under normal atmospheric conditions**__.

 __
 
• These gases are **hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, chlorine, helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon**.
 
• The periodic table is managed by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, or IUPAC.
 
• The modern periodic table sorts the elements according to increasing atomic number instead of increasing atomic mass.
 
• There are **118 elements** in a periodic table.
 
• There are seven periods and eighteen groups in the modern periodic table.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **size of the atoms (atomic size) **decreases as we move from left to right in a period.
 
• The **metallic properties of elements** decrease while the non-metallic properties increase as we move from left to right in a period.
 
• **Atoms** increase in size (or increase in atomic size) as you move down a group of the periodic table.
 
• The metallic properties of elements increase as we move down the group of the periodic table.

questions.question: _______ is a branch of biology that studies fungi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mycology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mycology is a branch of biology that studies fungi**__.

 __
 
• Fungi are unicellular or multicellular thick-cell-walled heterotroph decomposers that eat decaying matter and form tangles of fibers.
 
• They use complex organic compounds as a source of energy and carbon, not photosynthesis.
 
• They are found in almost any habitat, but live mostly on land, primarily on soil or plant material rather than in sea or freshwater.
 
• A small number of fungi cause diseases in animals.
 
• In humans, fungal diseases include skin diseases such as athlete's foot, ringworm, and thrush.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morphology **is the branch of biology that deals with the form of living organisms, and with relationships between their structures.
 
• **Kalology is **the branch of philosophy dealing with taste and the study of beauty in nature and art.
 
• **Virology **is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the biology of viruses and viral diseases.

questions.question: _______ is a practice of establishing and managing individual trees generally for amenity purposes.
questions.solution:

__

This is done to meet the diverse needs and values of landowners and society such as wildlife habitat, timber, water resources, restoration, and recreation on a sustainable basis.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the metals used in LED semiconductor technology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gallium**__.

__
 
• **Gallium is one of the metals used in LED semiconductor technology**__.

 __
 
• A light-emitting diode (LED) is a semiconductor light source that emits light when current is passed through it.
 
• Gallium is the first and primary element used in the manufacture of almost all semiconductor LED devices.
 
• Gallium is a metallic material found as a trace element in coal, bauxite and other minerals.
 
• The symbol for gallium is "Ga" - (atomic number 31).
 
• The specialty semiconductors used for LED manufacturing are **gallium arsenide (GaAs), gallium phosphide (GaP), or gallium arsenide phosphide (GaAsP**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indium gallium nitride (InGaN): blue, green and ultraviolet high-brightness LEDs
 
• Aluminum gallium indium phosphide (AlGaInP): yellow, orange and red high-brightness LEDs
 
• Aluminum gallium arsenide (AlGaAs): red and infrared LEDs

questions.question: The elements of the groups 3 to 12 are called _______ elements or transition elements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**d-block**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elements from groups 3 to 12 are called d-block elements or transition elements**__.

 __
 
• As a group, they exhibit typical metallic properties and are less reactive than metals in groups 1 and 2.
 
• The term 'transition' refers to the fact that the d sublevel, which is in the process of filling, is at a lower principal energy level than the s sublevel previously filled.
 
• The electrons of transition metals can participate in the formation of chemical bonds - in two shells instead of just one.
 
• Transition metal compounds that dissolve in water exhibit a wide variety of bright colors.
 
• As visible light passes through a transition metal compound dissolved in water, the d-orbitals absorb light of different energies.
 
• Visible light of a given energy level that is not absorbed produces a solution of a specific colour.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The modern periodic table sorts the elements according to increasing atomic number instead of increasing atomic mass.
 
• There are **118 elements in a periodic table**.
 
• There are seven periods and eighteen groups in the modern periodic table.
